Copenhagen Housing Monitor

Live-listing indicators for Copenhagen + Frederiksberg, snapshotted weekly from Boliga. Asking prices, cuts and days-on-market are leading indicators; realised sold prices are the lagging ground truth.

“Est. sold /m²” is the median price per m² of comparable sold homes (same district, property type, ±25% size and, where possible, same rooms). “vs comps” is how far asking sits above (+) or below (−) that — asking is normally a few % above realised sales, so treat small positives as normal. Co-op (andel) listings, foreclosures and rows with an implausible price/m² are excluded; “n=” flags low comp counts. The “Why cheap?” column now surfaces visible reasons from each listing's detail page — poor energy class, leasehold land, a ground floor, or a stale listing. A big negative “vs comps” with a ✓ clean tag is the genuinely interesting one; tick “Hide flagged” to hunt those. Detail is fetched a few hundred listings per week (candidates first), so some rows read pending… until enriched. Balcony/condition aren't in Boliga's data — they're only in the agent's description behind the link. “Listed” is when the listing went live (sorted newest-first by default); a NEW tag marks the last 7 days — though an agent re-listing a stale flat can reset that date, so an occasional “new” is really a re-list. “Open house” is the next public showing (åbent hus) straight from Boliga's feed — pick a date in the filter to see only flats showing that day. It refreshes every run, but only ~half of listings publish a showing date, and times are shown as Boliga lists them — always confirm on the listing before turning up. The 📅 next to an upcoming showing opens Google Calendar with the event pre-filled; pick which calendar (e.g. your shared one) from the dropdown before saving. Even clean, this is a screen to shortlist and inspect, not a valuation.

Map — listings & viewings

Areas
Showing today Upcoming showing No showing date

Pins come straight from Boliga's coordinates (every listing has them). Colour shows whether a public showing is booked. Click a pin for the address, price, showing time, a 📅 add-to-calendar link and the listing. The map is the only part of the app that loads anything from the internet — if it can't (no connection, or blocked), you'll see a notice here and every other tab keeps working.

Sold prices — 3,778 archived sales

Areas
SoldDistrictAddressm²Rooms Sold priceSold /m²vs ask

These are realised sale prices from the public land registry — what buyers actually paid — for a specific apartment (full address). “vs ask” shows how far below the original asking price it sold, when the feed provides it. Sales register ~1–3 months after closing, so the most recent weeks are still filling in. Search a street to see what nearby flats fetched.

Saved & tracked

Nothing saved yet. Tap the ☆ on any listing in For sale or Sold and it shows up here — then we track what it eventually sells for versus the asking you saved.

AreaAddressm²Your asking Sold forΔ vs askStatus

Matched by address against the weekly sold archive, so a sale shows up here within a week or two of registering (land-registry lag). “Your asking” is the price captured the moment you starred it; “Sold for” is the realised price; “Δ vs ask” is how far below (−) or above the asking it actually sold. Stars live in this browser only.

Asking vs. sold — the key distinction. Asking = what sellers list live listings at (leading, updates weekly). Sold (realised) = what homes actually changed hands for, from the land registry (lagging ~1–3 months). Asking normally sits a few % above sold. For "going rates in a neighbourhood", read the sold column.

Market direction (weekly trend)

Read this before trusting a trend. Asking prices are what sellers want, not what they get; realised sold prices lag ~1-3 months. District tags are by postcode (approximate). The source (Boliga) is an undocumented scrape that can drift. A single snapshot shows no direction — several consistent weeks do. Cross-check quarterly against official Finans Danmark / Danmarks Statistik figures before any decision that matters.
